page.title: Eight steps, then you file
page.intro: This is a Champaign / Illinois screener for tax year 2025 — not a filed return. Click a dotted blue word anytime you want more detail.
page.blueHelp: Those links open a short explanation of the tax idea and how to answer. Close it by clicking the word again.

intro.title: Filing Illinois taxes without the panic
intro.lead: If you had a campus job, internship, side hustle, or first full-time paycheck in 2025 and you lived around Champaign, this walkthrough is for you. KEENFinance does not file for you. It lines up the questions, forms, and official links so you can file with confidence.
intro.heroSpeech: Filing Illinois taxes without the panic. If you had a campus job, internship, side hustle, or first full-time paycheck in 2025 and you lived around Champaign, this walkthrough is for you. KEENFinance does not file for you. It lines up the questions, forms, and official links so you can file with confidence.
intro.yes1: You earned money in 2025 — wages, tips, gig pay, interest, or unemployment.
intro.yes2: You lived in Illinois for all or part of 2025, including as a student in Champaign.
intro.yes3: You are a young adult and a parent might still claim you. You may still need to file.
intro.yes4: You want to check credits like the earned income credit, student-loan interest, or Illinois work credits.
intro.yes5: You have not already filed an original 2025 return.
intro.pauseIf: Pause and get extra help if…
intro.pause1: You moved between states, had gig expenses, crypto, rentals, or Marketplace insurance (Form 1095-A).
intro.pause2: You already filed, or you need someone to click Submit — that happens at IRS, MyTax Illinois, or a VITA site.
intro.filingSpeech: Is filing taxes for me? Yes, if you earned money in 2025, lived in Illinois for all or part of 2025, might still be claimed by a parent, want to check credits, and have not already filed an original 2025 return. Pause and get extra help if you moved between states, had gig expenses, crypto, rentals, or Marketplace insurance, or if you already filed.
intro.happens1: You are reporting money earned in calendar year 2025. Most people file two returns: a federal Form 1040 and an Illinois IL-1040. Illinois starts from federal income, then uses its own exemptions. The state rate for 2025 is 4.95%. The usual filing and payment date is April 15, 2026. An extension (if you still qualify) generally moves the paperwork deadline, not the payment deadline.
intro.happens2: Living in Champaign today does not automatically mean you were a full-year Illinois resident in 2025. If you moved, worked in another state, or are on a visa, we will flag that as “review needed” and still give you a document list.
intro.happensSpeech: What actually happens. You are reporting money earned in calendar year 2025. Most people file a federal Form 1040 and an Illinois IL-1040. The state rate for 2025 is 4.95 percent. The usual filing and payment date is April 15, 2026. Living in Champaign today does not automatically mean you were a full-year Illinois resident in 2025.
intro.rolesH2: What we do, and what you do
intro.keenBody: Walk you through residency, household, income, and possible credits. Build a personalized checklist. Point to official 2025 forms. Explain benefits in plain language — never as a promised refund.
intro.youBody: Gather the real W-2s and 1099s, confirm the facts, then file on IRS Free File, MyTax Illinois, or with a free VITA helper. Do not enter a real SSN or bank login here — this is a guide, not the government.
intro.rolesSpeech: What we do, and what you do. KEENFinance walks you through residency, household, income, and possible credits, and builds a checklist. You gather the real forms, confirm the facts, then file on IRS Free File, MyTax Illinois, or with a free VITA helper. Do not enter a real Social Security number or bank login here.
intro.creditBody: Lowers tax you owe. Some credits can increase a refund.
intro.deductionBody: Taken off income before tax is calculated. It is not cash handed to you.
intro.withholdingBody: Tax already taken from your paycheck.
intro.eligibleBody: Our supported checks passed based on what you confirmed. It is not a filed, reviewed, or accepted return.
intro.wordsSpeech: Words you will see. A credit lowers tax you owe. A deduction is taken off income before tax is calculated. Withholding is tax already taken from your paycheck. Appears eligible means our supported checks passed. It is not a filed return.
intro.readyBody: Next you will answer a short checklist. Each circle turns into a green check when that step is done. Pick one path at a time — if you change your mind, the other subtab closes. At the end you get a recap of what you told us and which official forms to use. Then you file for real.
intro.readySpeech: Ready when you are. Next you will answer a short checklist. Each circle turns into a green check when that step is done. At the end you get a recap and official forms. Then you file for real.
intro.cta: I'm ready to file my taxes!

nav.6: Checklist and how you will file

1.h2: Gather payer documents — or skip ahead
1.p1: IRS and Illinois want forms from whoever paid you, not a screenshot of your checking app. Upload what you already have, or skip and we will build a list as you answer. A blank IRS PDF is not a substitute for an employer
1.w2Help: A W-2 is the year-end form your employer prepares. It shows wages and tax already withheld. Get it from payroll. If it never arrives, ask them first; Form 4852 is a last-resort substitute, not a homemade W-2.
1.uploadDetail: Opens 1a. Upload a PDF, review its values, then save to your profile.
1.skipDetail: Marks step 1 complete. You can still upload later by reopening this step.
1.speech: Step 1. Gather payer documents, or skip ahead. The IRS and Illinois want forms from whoever paid you, not a screenshot of your checking app. Upload what you already have, or skip and we will build a list as you answer. A blank IRS PDF is not a substitute for an employer W-2. A W-2 shows wages and tax withheld. Get it from payroll.

1a.h2: Upload what the payer sent you
1a.p: Only attach copies you actually received. Click a form name to open a practice copy, fill the blanks one by one, then finish. A green check means that form is complete. A red X means it is missing or still has required blanks. Nothing here is sent to the IRS.
1a.done: I have what I need for now
1a.speech: Step 1a. Click a form name to open a practice PDF. Fill the blanks one by one. A green check means the form is complete. A red X means it is missing or still has required blanks.

2.p1: We are preparing money earned in calendar year 2025, usually filed in 2026. Living in Champaign today does not prove you were a full-year
2.residentHelp: Full-year residents generally file a resident IL-1040. If you moved or worked in another state, Illinois may need Schedule NR. Answer based on 2025, not where your mail goes now.
2.p2: . Answer Yes / No / Not sure — “not sure” is stored as unknown, not as No.
2.qYear: Are we preparing taxes for money you earned in 2025?
2.qResidentHelp: Tax residency is not the same as a Champaign mailing address or an immigration label. If you are unsure, pick Not sure. We will flag review instead of guessing.
2.qResidentPre: Are you a U.S. citizen or
2.qFiled: Did you already file your 2025 return?
2.qExt: If you have not filed, did you request an on-time extension?
2.fullTitle: I lived in Illinois all of 2025
2.fullDetail: Opens 2a. Typical for a Champaign student or worker who did not move mid-year.
2.movedTitle: I moved or also worked in another state
2.movedDetail: Opens 2b and closes 2a. Part-year / nonresident cases need extra review.
2.speech: Step 2. Lock tax year 2025 and Illinois. We are preparing money earned in calendar year 2025, usually filed in 2026. Living in Champaign today does not prove you were a full-year Illinois resident. Answer yes, no, or not sure. Not sure is stored as unknown, not as no.

2a.p1: You will usually prepare a federal
2a.f1040Help: Your main federal income tax return. 2025 forms are labeled 2025 — confirm the printed year before you file.
2a.il1040Help: Your Illinois income tax return. Illinois starts from federal income, then applies its own exemptions. For ordinary 2025 cases the personal exemption is $2,850 per eligible person. The state rate is 4.95%. We still will not invent a refund.
2a.p3: . Ordinary filing and payment date: April 15, 2026. An extension generally moves paperwork, not the payment date.
2a.speech: Step 2a. Full-year Illinois resident. You will usually prepare a federal Form 1040 and a resident IL-1040. Illinois starts from federal income. The ordinary filing and payment date is April 15, 2026.

2b.p1: This is not “you cannot file.” It means our supported residency rules stop here. Part-year and nonresident Illinois filers often add
2b.nrHelp: Illinois Schedule NR splits income among states. Use software or a VITA volunteer for the split. Keep collecting documents in this checklist.
2b.states: Which other state(s), if you remember?
2b.done: Keep my document list and continue
2b.speech: Step 2b. Moved or multi-state. This is review needed, not you cannot file. Part-year and nonresident Illinois filers often add Schedule NR.

3.h2: Who counts in your tax household
3.p1: Use December 31, 2025 for marriage. Dates, not today’s age, drive the rules. “Single parent” is not automatically
3.hohHelp: Head of household has extra tests: unmarried or considered unmarried, a qualifying person, and paying more than half the home’s upkeep. Dependent parents living elsewhere have their own rules. We only screen; Pub 501 has the official tests.
3.p2: . Do not type a real SSN — identifier type is enough for this demo.
3.dob: Your date of birth (age rules use this date, not how old you feel today)
3.blindHelp: Totally blind, or certified limits of 20/200 or a 20-degree field in the better eye with correction. Confirm; do not infer this from using a screen reader or large text.
3.qBlindPre: Do you meet the tax definition of
3.qKids: Do you have children or other people you may claim?
3.childCount: How many people might you claim? (not everyone who lives with you qualifies)
3.childDob: Date of birth (federal child credit generally needs under 17 at year-end; Illinois child credit uses under 12)
3.months: Months they lived with you in 2025
3.indepDetail: Opens 3a. Needed for several credits, including federal childless EITC.
3.depTitle: A parent or someone else might claim me
3.depDetail: Opens 3b. Common for students. You may still need to file.
3.speech: Step 3. Who counts in your tax household. Use December 31, 2025 for marriage. Dates, not today’s age, drive the rules. Single parent is not automatically head of household. Do not type a real Social Security number.

3a.p1: Confirm with anyone who claimed you last year. If you can be claimed as a
3a.depHelp: Living with someone is not enough. Different credits use different tests. Dependents also use a different standard-deduction worksheet — we will not auto-grant the full $15,750 single amount.
3a.p2: , federal childless EITC usually fails even if Illinois expanded EITC might still be screened.
3a.speech: Step 3a. Filing as independent. Confirm with anyone who claimed you last year. If you can be claimed as a dependent, federal childless EITC usually fails even if Illinois expanded EITC might still be screened.

3b.p: Record two facts separately: could someone claim you, and did they? Those answers feed different benefits. Talk so you do not both e-file conflicting statuses.
3b.qCould: Could someone else claim you on their 2025 return?
3b.qDid: Did they actually claim you (if you know)?
3b.speech: Step 3b. You might be a dependent. Record two facts separately: could someone claim you, and did they?

4.h2: What kinds of income showed up
4.p: Do not guess taxable wages from a Venmo or paycheck deposit. Use the payer form. Pick the closest path — you can still list extra types inside it. Amounts you submit here are facts you confirmed, not a refund estimate.
4.w2Detail: Campus job, internship, or hourly work with an employer.
4.gigDetail: Opens 4b. Self-employment tax and expenses need review.
4.mixTitle: A mix, or I am not sure
4.mixDetail: Wages plus interest, unemployment, or a side job.
4.speech: Step 4. What kinds of income showed up. Do not guess taxable wages from a deposit. Use the payer form. Pick the closest path: mostly a W-2 job, gig or 1099, or a mix.

4a.p: Collect every W-2. Missing one? Ask payroll first. We will not treat a net deposit as wages.
4a.speech: Step 4a. W-2 wages. Collect every W-2. If one is missing, ask payroll first. We will not treat a net deposit as wages.

4b.p: Platforms may send a 1099, but you still report all self-employment income. We will not invent deductions from transaction labels — keep notes and mark review if you had expenses.
4b.speech: Step 4b. Gig and 1099 income. Platforms may send a 1099, but you still report all self-employment income. We will not invent deductions from transaction labels.

4c.p1: Check every type that applies. Keep
4c.earnedHelp: Pay from work, including wages and many gig earnings. EITC compares earned income and AGI separately against a ceiling. Being under the ceiling is not enough by itself.
4c.speech: Step 4c. Mixed income. Check every type that applies. Keep earned income separate from bank interest.

4x.foreign: Did you receive any foreign income or file Form 2555?
4x.wages: Wages from W-2s (optional). Use plus or minus then Submit. Unknown is better than a guess.
4x.other: Other work or gig income you already know from forms
4x.eitcHelp: Earned Income Tax Credit. Investment income must be $11,950 or less for 2025. We screen; we do not compute your credit.

5.p1: We show separate federal and Illinois cards. Labels mean
5.eligibleHelp: Supported checks passed on facts you confirmed. It is not a reviewed, filed, or accepted return.
5.moreHelp: A required fact is missing, unclear, or contradictory. Missing is not No.
5.reviewHelp: Outside our rules (moves, gigs, Marketplace insurance, custody fights). Keep the checklist.
5.p2: . A published maximum is not your award. Amount not calculated until a real engine runs. Do not add credits and deductions into “your refund.”
5.simpleTitle: Simple: job, maybe rent, no kids
5.simpleDetail: Standard deduction and possible federal/Illinois EITC screening.
5.schoolTitle: School, student loans, or retirement savings
5.schoolDetail: 1098-E, education credits, Saver’s Credit (students often excluded).
5.kidsTitle: Kids, childcare, or an Illinois home I own
5.kidsDetail: Child credits, care, property tax, K–12 fees. Renters skip property tax credit.
5.speech: Step 5. Which extra story is closest? We show separate federal and Illinois cards. Appears eligible means supported checks passed. A published maximum is not your award.

5a.p1: For ordinary independent single filers, the 2025 federal
5a.stdHelp: $15,750 single or married filing separately; $31,500 joint; $23,625 head of household. It lowers income used to compute tax — it is not money paid to you. Age 65+ or qualifying blindness can add $2,000 (single/HOH) or $1,600 (married categories). Dependents use a different worksheet.
5a.p2: is $15,750. Rent does not create the Illinois property tax credit. A 22-year-old may fail federal childless EITC on age (generally 25–64) and still be screened for Illinois expanded EITC (ages 18–24 without a child).
5a.c1b: Needs earned income and AGI under the table for your filing status and qualifying children, investment income ≤ $11,950, and other tests. Childless filers generally need age 25–64 and cannot be someone else’s dependent. Amount not calculated.
5a.c2l: Evaluate even if federal is no
5a.c2b: Ordinary Illinois EITC is 20% of federal EITC. Expanded coverage can include qualifying ITIN filers and workers 18–24 or 65+ without a child. Use the state worksheet — do not return zero only because federal EITC is zero.
5a.speech: Step 5a. Simple W-2 screening. For ordinary independent single filers, the 2025 federal standard deduction is $15,750. Rent does not create the Illinois property tax credit. A 22-year-old may fail federal childless EITC on age and still be screened for Illinois expanded EITC.

5b.p: Loan interest and college tuition are different branches. A 1098-T alone does not prove an education credit.
5b.qLoan: Did you pay student-loan interest (not just principal)?
5b.loanAmt: Qualified interest you paid in 2025 (max we screen is $2,500)
5b.ableHelp: Your contributions may feed the Saver’s Credit. Employer match and rollovers do not count. Full-time students during any part of five calendar months are generally excluded.
5b.qRetPre: Did you put your own money into a retirement plan or
5b.c1b: Smaller of qualified interest paid or $2,500. 2025 phaseout MAGI $85,000–$100,000 if not joint. Excludes many MFS and claimed-dependent cases. Claim through Schedule 1.
5b.c2b: AOTC up to $2,500 per eligible student (first four postsecondary years). LLC up to $2,000 per return. Do not claim both for the same student. Form 8863.
5b.c3b: 2025 AGI ceilings include $39,500 single. Rates 10/20/50% on up to $2,000 of eligible contributions per person. Form 8880. Amount not calculated.
5b.speech: Step 5b. School, loans, and savings. Loan interest and college tuition are different branches. A 1098-T alone does not prove an education credit.

5c.h2: Kids, care, or a home you own
5c.p: Federal child credit generally needs a child under 17 at year-end. Illinois child credit is 40% of Illinois EITC for an eligible child under 12 — not a flat amount per kid. A home bought in 2025 generally cannot create the 2025 property tax credit. Renters skip it.
5c.qCare: Did you pay someone to care for a child or other person so you could work or look for work?
5c.qK12: Did you pay Illinois K–12 tuition, book fees, or lab fees?
5c.qHome: Did you own and live in an Illinois home in 2024, and pay its property taxes in 2025?
5c.propAmt: Eligible Illinois property tax paid in 2025 (credit is generally 5% of this, limited by state tax)
5c.c1b: 2025 CTC maximum $2,200 per qualifying child; refundable ACTC portion up to $1,700 subject to calculation. Do not add them as two independent awards.
5c.c2b: Need the bill, payment proof, and parcel number (Champaign County Treasurer if local). Penalties and non-residence portions do not count.
5c.c3l: 25% of qualified costs above $250, max $750 total
5c.c3b: Not per child. After-school care and ordinary supplies do not automatically qualify.
5c.speech: Step 5c. Kids, care, or a home you own. Federal child credit generally needs a child under 17 at year-end. Illinois child credit is 40 percent of Illinois EITC for an eligible child under 12. Renters skip the property tax credit.

5d.p: “We have not checked this benefit” is different from “you cannot claim it.” Take 1095-A, gig records, or overtime stubs to software or VITA.
5d.qTips: Qualifying tips or FLSA overtime premium in 2025?
5d.c1b: Advance premium tax credit must be reconciled. Missing this can stall e-file.
5d.c2b: 2025 caps: tips $25,000 per return; overtime $12,500 nonjoint / $25,000 joint. Do not assume Illinois copies the federal deduction. Amount not calculated.
5d.speech: Step 5d. Review needed, still useful. We have not checked this benefit is different from you cannot claim it. Take 1095-A, gig records, or overtime stubs to software or VITA.

6.h2: How do you want to file for real?
6.p: KEENFinance stops at a preparation summary. You still submit the 1040 and IL-1040 yourself (or with a volunteer). Only one subtab stays open.
6.selfDetail: Official 2025 PDFs, MyTax Illinois, IRS Free File.
6.waitTitle: I already filed, or I am waiting on forms
6.waitDetail: Do not file a second original return.
6.speech: Step 6. How do you want to file for real? KEENFinance stops at a preparation summary. You still submit the 1040 and IL-1040 yourself or with a volunteer.

6a.p: Use 2025 Form 1040 and IL-1040. Confirm the printed year. Field helpers on those sites should cite the form name, year, line label, and your confirmed value — never invent a missing box.
6a.speech: Step 6a. File it yourself. Use 2025 Form 1040 and IL-1040. Confirm the printed year.

6c.p: If a 2025 original return is already in, you need an amendment — not a second 1040. Still waiting on a W-2? Ask payroll before Form 4852.
6c.speech: Step 6c. Pause before another return. If a 2025 original return is already in, you need an amendment, not a second 1040.

7.h2: Benefits this walkthrough says you may qualify for
7.p: These are screening results from your answers — not an award, not a refund, and not tax advice. “Appears eligible” only means the supported questions pointed this way. Amounts are not calculated here.
7.speech: Step 7. Benefits you may qualify for. These are screening results from your answers, not an award and not a refund. Amounts are not calculated here.

8.h2: What you built — not a filed return
8.p: Preparation summary for tax year 2025. “Appears eligible” only means our supported questions were answered. No refund total is shown.
8.next: Next action: take this list to Form 1040 and MyTax Illinois. Ordinary 2025 deadline: April 15, 2026.
8.speech: Step 8. What you built is a preparation summary, not a filed return. Appears eligible only means our supported questions were answered. No refund total is shown. Ordinary 2025 deadline is April 15, 2026.

w2.name: Form W-2
w2.summary: Job wages and withholding. Employer/payroll portal; request a replacement if missing.

employeeName.label: Your name as shown on the W-2
employeeName.help: Find the employee section (usually boxes c/e on the left). Type the name exactly as payroll printed it — first, middle initial, last — even if you go by a nickname or a different spelling on campus. This is who the IRS thinks earned these wages.

employerName.label: Employer name
employerName.help: This is the business that paid you, usually in box c. Campus jobs often list the university, a department, or a staffing vendor — not your supervisor’s name. If you had two jobs, you need a separate W-2 for each employer.

ein.label: Employer EIN (box b)
ein.help: The Employer Identification Number is a 9-digit tax ID for the business, usually formatted like 12-3456789, in box b near the employer name. It is not your Social Security number. If this demo copy is blank, type the number from the original W-2 or ask payroll for a replacement — do not invent one.

wages.label: Box 1 — wages, tips, other compensation
wages.help: Box 1 is your taxable wages for the year, not the amount that hit your bank account. Copy the dollar amount with cents (for example 36000.00). Do not copy box 3 or box 5 into this field; those Social Security and Medicare wages can be different. A blank box 1 is missing information, not automatically zero.

federalWithheld.label: Box 2 — federal income tax withheld
federalWithheld.help: Box 2 is federal income tax already sent to the IRS from this job. Copy the printed amount. If nothing was withheld, enter 0.00 only when you are sure the box is meant to be zero — do not copy Illinois tax from boxes 17–19, and do not reuse a number from a different sample W-2.

ssWages.label: Box 3 — Social Security wages
ssWages.help: Box 3 is wages counted for Social Security tax. It is often close to box 1 but not always (tips, retirement, or wage-base limits can change it). Copy what is printed. If your copy is empty, leave this optional field blank rather than guessing.

stateWages.label: Box 16 — state wages
stateWages.help: Box 16 is wages this employer reported to a state, usually Illinois on a Champaign job. Copy the amount next to the state name. If you also worked in another state, keep that W-2 separate instead of adding the numbers here.

nec.name: 1099-NEC / 1099-K / 1099-MISC
nec.summary: Side jobs and platforms, plus your own income/expense notes.

payerName.label: Payer or platform name
payerName.help: This is who paid you for freelance, gig, or contract work — a client, app, or marketplace — printed in the payer box on the left. Use that legal name, not a nickname or the name of the person who messaged you in the app.

recipientName.label: Your name on the form
recipientName.help: Copy your name from the recipient section. It must match what the payer has on file. If it is blank on a practice copy, type your legal name as it should appear on a tax return.

compensation.label: Nonemployee compensation (box 1)
compensation.help: Box 1 on Form 1099-NEC is the gross amount they paid you before you subtract expenses. Enter dollars and cents. This is not automatically profit, and a blank box 1 is not zero — if the copy is empty, fill the real amount from the original form or your payment records.

federalWithheld.label: Federal income tax withheld
federalWithheld.help: Box 4 is tax the payer already sent to the IRS. Gig and freelance forms are often blank here. Leave it empty if nothing was withheld, or enter 0.00 if the form shows zero. Do not copy state tax into this box.

stateIncome.label: State income reported
stateIncome.help: If the form shows state income (often on the right), copy that amount. If that area is empty, leave this optional field blank. Do not invent Illinois wages from your bank deposits.

int.name: 1099-INT
int.summary: Bank interest. Download from the bank tax-document portal.

payerName.label: Bank or payer name
payerName.help: This is the bank, credit union, or broker that paid interest, in the payer box. Use the institution name on the form, not the nickname of the checking product.

recipientName.label: Your name on the account
recipientName.help: Copy the name in the recipient box. On a joint account it may list one owner or both. If this practice copy left the name blank, type the name that belongs on the account — do not leave a required identity field empty.

interest.label: Box 1 — interest income
interest.help: Box 1 is ordinary interest credited during 2025 (for example 84.50). Even small amounts can still go on a return. Copy the printed figure. A blank box 1 is missing data, not a silent zero, unless you confirm the account earned nothing.

federalWithheld.label: Box 4 — federal tax withheld
federalWithheld.help: Box 4 is backup withholding, which most student accounts never have. If the box is empty, leave this optional field blank. If it shows an amount, copy it exactly.

e.name: 1098-E
e.summary: Student-loan interest. Interest under $600 can still count even without this form.

lenderName.label: Lender or servicer
lenderName.help: This is the company that collected your student-loan payments and sent the 1098-E. It may be a servicer, not the school and not the original lender you remember from freshman year. Copy the name in the lender box.

borrowerName.label: Borrower name
borrowerName.help: The borrower is the student legally responsible for the loan. Parents who only helped pay should not put their own name here unless they are the borrower on the form.

loanInterest.label: Box 1 — student loan interest received
loanInterest.help: Box 1 is interest you paid in 2025, not the remaining loan balance and not the monthly payment. Copy dollars and cents. If you paid interest but never received a 1098-E because it was under $600, you can still enter the interest from your servicer statement.

t.name: 1098-T
t.summary: College tuition billed. You still need what you actually paid and any grants.

schoolName.label: College or school name
schoolName.help: This is the school that billed tuition — Champaign students often see University of Illinois. Copy the institution name from the 1098-T header, not the name of a single class or professor.

studentName.label: Student name
studentName.help: The student the 1098-T is for. If this is your return, that should be you. A parent filing separately would use the student’s form only if they are allowed to claim the education credit.

tuition.label: Payments received for qualified tuition
tuition.help: Most schools now report box 1 (payments received). Some still report box 2 (amounts billed). Copy the box your form actually fills. This is not automatically the education credit — scholarships and what you personally paid still matter.

grants.label: Scholarships or grants
grants.help: Box 5 is scholarships or grants the school administered. Copy it even if you think aid was “free money.” Grants can reduce an education credit, so skipping a filled box 5 can overstate a credit later.

g.name: 1099-G
g.summary: Unemployment from the issuing state agency’s document portal.

agencyName.label: Payer (state agency)
agencyName.help: Unemployment is paid by a state agency, not your old employer. Copy the payer name from the 1099-G. For Illinois claims this is usually the state unemployment office.

recipientName.label: Your name
recipientName.help: Copy the name on the unemployment claim. It should match the person who received the payments.

unemployment.label: Box 1 — unemployment compensation
unemployment.help: Box 1 is taxable unemployment paid to you in 2025. Copy the annual total, not a single weekly deposit. Unemployment is usually taxable even if no tax was withheld.

federalWithheld.label: Box 4 — federal tax withheld
federalWithheld.help: Only some people elect withholding on unemployment. If box 4 is empty, leave this optional field blank. If it has an amount, copy it; that tax already went to the IRS.

a.name: 1095-A
a.summary: Marketplace health coverage. Required if you had advance premium credits.

marketplaceName.label: Marketplace name
marketplaceName.help: This is Healthcare.gov or the state marketplace that sent Form 1095-A. It is not employer coverage from a W-2 job and not a campus clinic bill. Copy the marketplace name from the form.

recipientName.label: Recipient name
recipientName.help: The recipient is the person the policy is issued to. Copy that name. Family members listed in the coverage table are additional information for a helper, not a replacement for this field.

premium.label: Monthly enrollment premium
premium.help: Use the premium column from the 1095-A (monthly rows or the annual total if you are entering one figure here). Do not mix this with employer health coverage or a campus insurance waiver.

advanceCredit.label: Advance payment of premium tax credit
advanceCredit.help: This is what the marketplace already paid toward your premium (the APTC column). Form 8962 later reconciles it with a helper. Enter the form amount. Missing this on a real return can stall e-file.

prior.name: Prior-year return
prior.summary: Helps match last year’s AGI if software asks. Optional.

taxYear.label: Tax year of that return
taxYear.help: Look at the year printed at the top of page 1. If you are preparing 2025, last year’s return is usually 2024. Do not type the year you are filing now unless that is actually the form in front of you.

filingName.label: Name on that return
filingName.help: Type your legal name as it appeared on that 1040, usually near the top of page 1. This helps match the person on the draft. A blank name on a practice 1040 means the form is still incomplete.

wagesNoted.label: Wages noted on that return (line 1a)
wagesNoted.help: If the old 1040 shows wages on line 1a, copy that amount for your notes. This optional field is a reminder of last year’s job income; it does not replace this year’s W-2.

taxableInterest.label: Taxable interest (line 2b)
taxableInterest.help: Line 2b is taxable interest from banks (the 1099-INT total that belongs on the 1040). Copy the printed amount. On this practice pack the draft 1040 leaves line 2b empty on purpose — enter the interest from your 1099-INT (for example 84.50) if you are completing the exercise.

docs.id: Photo ID and your filing address for 2025.
docs.files: Files already attached in this tab: {{names}}.
docs.none: Payer forms still to collect (nothing uploaded yet).
docs.w2: Form W-2 from each employer — payroll portal or a replacement from HR.
docs.gig: 1099-NEC/K/MISC plus your own income/expense log. Gig totals are not automatic write-offs.
docs.unemp: Form 1099-G from the state unemployment site.
docs.e: Form 1098-E or a servicer year-end interest statement.
docs.t: Form 1098-T, the bursar ledger, and which costs you actually paid.
docs.ret: Year-end contribution record (W-2 box 12 or account statement).
docs.care: Childcare provider statement with expenses and identifying details (W-10 if you need their tax ID).
docs.k12: Itemized K–12 tuition, book, or lab receipts — not ordinary school supplies.
docs.home: Illinois property tax bill, proof of 2025 payment, and parcel number (Champaign County Treasurer if local).
docs.mkt: Form 1095-A from the Marketplace — required before many e-files go through.
docs.tips: Pay stubs that separate tips or FLSA overtime premium.
docs.kids: Child/dependent facts on file: {{count}} person(s). Bring relationship, support, and identifier-type details — not SSNs in this demo.
docs.forms: Federal Form 1040 and Illinois IL-1040. Add Schedule EIC, 8812, IL-E/EITC, ICR, 8880, 2441, 8863, or 1-A only if that branch applied.

benefits.likely: Appears eligible based on your answers
benefits.maybe: Possible — a tax helper should confirm
benefits.empty: Answer the earlier steps so we can list matching credits. Nothing is awarded here.
benefits.disclaimer: KEENFinance does not calculate a refund. Take this list to IRS Free File, MyTax Illinois, or a VITA site.

std.title: Standard deduction
std.body: Most student and first-job returns use the standard deduction instead of itemizing. Your exact amount depends on filing status.

ilExempt.title: Illinois personal exemption
ilExempt.body: Illinois starts from federal income, then applies its own exemptions. Full-year residents usually claim this on IL-1040.

eitc.title: Earned Income Credit (EITC)
eitc.body: A refundable credit for people who worked. You can qualify with or without children, but income and filing-status tests apply.

ilEitc.title: Illinois Earned Income Credit
ilEitc.body: Illinois has a matching earned-income credit. It follows the federal EITC idea and is claimed on the Illinois return.

ctc.title: Child tax credit / other dependent credit
ctc.body: Possible if you have a qualifying child or dependent. Age, residency, and support tests still have to be met on the real return.

care.title: Child and dependent care credit
care.body: You paid for care so you could work or look for work. Keep the provider’s identifying details — not in this demo.

education.title: Education credit (American Opportunity or Lifetime Learning)
education.body: Tuition and required fees may qualify. Scholarships on Form 1098-T can reduce the credit. A helper should pick which credit fits.

loan.title: Student-loan interest deduction
loan.body: Interest you paid on a qualified student loan, even if no 1098-E arrived because the amount was under $600.

saver.title: Saver’s Credit
saver.body: A credit for retirement contributions. Full-time students are often excluded, so treat this as a maybe until a helper checks.

property.title: Illinois property tax credit
property.body: Homeowners who paid 2025 Illinois property tax may get a credit. Renters skip this. Bring the bill and proof of payment.

k12.title: Illinois K–12 education expense credit
k12.body: Qualified K–12 tuition, books, or lab fees — not ordinary school supplies.

premium.title: Premium tax credit (Form 8962)
premium.body: Required if you had Marketplace coverage with advance credits. You need Form 1095-A before most e-files will go through.

tips.title: Tip and overtime reporting
tips.body: Tips belong on the return even if they were not on a W-2. Keep pay stubs that separate tips.

review.title: Human review flagged
review.body: You chose a path that needs a person — Marketplace, extra complexity, or similar. Use VITA or a trusted preparer before you file.
